newsitem.title: USA: Ahmanson sees $400 mln restructuring charge.
newsitem.headline: Ahmanson sees $400 mln restructuring charge.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson and Co said it expects to incur a restructuring charge and acquisition costs of $400 million in the event its proposed $6.5 billion bid for Great Western Financial Corp succeeds.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the nation's largest thrift said it would expect to incur the charge, which is about equal to one year of estimated cost savings from the merger.
In addition, Ahmanson expects that the combined company may need to take an additional provision for loan losses of up to $150 million.
Madeline Kleiner, senior executive vice president and general counsel, said the company believes it is possible the merger could be consummated by the third quarter.
The restructuring charge would be taken upon closing of the deal.

In the filing, Ahmanson also said it currently estimates that the revenue growth of the combined company would exceed any revenues losse associated with the consolidations, although there can be no assurances that some revenues will not be lost.
